title: Phases of the menstrual cycle
answer: The menstrual cycle has a few stages that repeat. First is your period, when the lining of the womb comes out as blood. Next, the lining starts to grow thick again while an egg gets ready in an ovary. Around the middle of the cycle, the egg is released (ovulation). After that, the body waits to see if a pregnancy starts. If it does not, hormone levels drop and the next period begins. The whole cycle usually takes about three to five weeks.

title: Hormones that control the cycle
answer: Your cycle is controlled by chemical messengers called hormones. The brain sends signals to the ovaries. The ovaries then make two main hormones: oestrogen, which helps the womb lining grow and an egg to mature, and progesterone, which keeps the lining ready after ovulation. When no pregnancy happens, these hormones fall and your period starts. Changes in these hormones can also affect your mood, skin and energy at different times of the month.

title: Why the womb lining sheds each month
answer: Each month the inside lining of your womb (uterus) grows thick and soft with blood and tissue. This is the body getting ready in case a pregnancy starts, because a fertilised egg would need that lining to grow. When no pregnancy happens, the body does not need the lining, so hormone levels drop and the lining breaks down. It leaves the body through the vagina as your period. Then a new lining starts to grow again.

title: What ovulation is
answer: Ovulation is when one of your ovaries releases a mature egg. The egg travels down a tube towards the womb. This usually happens once in each cycle, often about two weeks before your next period starts, but the exact day differs between people and from month to month. The egg lives for about one day. Ovulation is a normal sign that your reproductive system is working, and it is the time when pregnancy is most possible if there is sex.

answer: Some girls notice signs around ovulation, but many notice nothing, and that is normal. Common signs include clear, wet, slippery discharge that stretches like raw egg white, a mild ache on one side of the lower belly, slightly tender breasts, or feeling more energetic. title: Fertile days in the cycle
answer: Your fertile days are the days in your cycle when pregnancy can happen if you have sex. Sperm can live inside the body for up to about five days, and the egg lives about one day, so the fertile time is roughly the five days before ovulation plus the day of ovulation. Because ovulation often moves from month to month, especially in young people, it is hard to know these days exactly. Counting days is not a safe way to avoid pregnancy for most young people; talk to a health worker about reliable methods.

It is a normal body fluid, just like sweat or saliva, and it leaves the body because the lining is not needed that month.

title: How many eggs a girl is born with
answer: A baby girl is born with all the eggs she will ever have, about one to two million, stored in her ovaries. Many naturally disappear over time, so by puberty there are a few hundred thousand left. Usually only one egg is released each cycle. Having periods does not make you run out of eggs quickly, and your supply lasts until menopause, many years later.

title: Do friends' periods sync
answer: Many girls believe that friends or sisters who live together start bleeding at the same time. Studies have not shown that this really happens. Because cycles are different lengths, periods often overlap by chance and then drift apart again. So if your period starts on the same day as your roommate, it is most likely a coincidence. Either way, it is normal and nothing to worry about.

You cannot hold it in like urine, which is why you use a pad or other product.

title: Does the period come on the same date every month
answer: Your period does not usually come on the same calendar date each month. It follows your cycle length, not the calendar. For example, if your cycle is 28 days and your period started on 3 March, the next one may start around 31 March. Many cycles also change by a few days from month to month, which is normal. Marking each start day helps you learn your own pattern.

title: Why the period comes earlier each calendar month
answer: If your cycle is shorter than the number of days in a month, your period will start a little earlier in the month each time. For example, with a 28-day cycle, a period that started on 10 June may start around 8 July and then about 5 August. This is normal and does not mean your periods are coming too often. It is simply how cycle days fit into calendar months.
